feed.title: Standardizing public key exposure classification for existing outputs

entry.title: Standardizing public key exposure classification for existing outputs
entry.summary:
The discussion centers around a proposed specification for classifying Bitcoin outputs based on the publication status of their corresponding public keys. This proposal addresses a gap left by existing Bitcoin Improvement Proposals (BIPs), specifically BIP 360 and BIP 361, which do not specify how to determine if an output's public key is exposed. The motivation behind this specification is to provide clarity in cases where it's essential to know whether an output is vulnerable due to its public key being accessible on-chain.
Presently, there is a significant variance in estimates of how much Bitcoin supply is exposed, ranging from 25% to over 34%. Such discrepancies are often the result of differing definitions rather than errors in measurement. Several points of contention arise frequently within the community, particularly regarding whether certain types of outputs, like Pay-to-Taproot (P2TR) or previously spent Pay-to-Public-Key-Hash (P2PKH) addresses, are considered exposed at rest or only upon spending. Additionally, there's ambiguity about outputs whose scripts remain undisclosed and keys revealed off-chain.
The proposed draft categorizes exposure levels into four distinct classifications: EXPOSED_AT_REST, EXPOSED_ON_SPEND, NOT_EXPOSED, and UNDETERMINED. It introduces guidelines to ensure that when data is insufficient for a clear classification, outputs should default to the higher exposure category to avoid underestimating security risks. Notably, the mechanism of disclosure doesn’t alter the classification; for example, a reused address that still holds a balance is classified similarly to a P2PK output as EXPOSED_AT_REST.
Furthermore, any output type not recognized by the classifier is automatically categorized as UNDETERMINED instead of being assumed as unexposed. This approach acknowledges the limitations of classifiers that might encounter new or unknown output types. A crucial aspect of the specification is the implementation of a constant-time floor rule, which helps prevent incorrect exposure classifications caused by incomplete historical data scans.
For more detailed information on the proposed exposure classification system, including its reference implementation and test vectors, you can refer to the following [GitHub repository](https://github.com/duncan0k/pubkey-exposure-classification). Additionally, further discussions and insights on this topic were shared on Delving Bitcoin, which can be accessed via this [link](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/standardizing-an-exposure-classification-for-existing-outputs-pre-bip/2866).
This initiative seeks wide feedback before further development, questioning whether such a specification is necessary or if it should be left to individual implementations. Moreover, there's an interest in identifying any prior art or existing standards that might have been overlooked in crafting this proposal.
